title: George W. Erving to James Madison, Madrid, 10 Aug 1807, private No. 24 'Duplicate', 'In Mr Pinkneys Cypher, the Cypher of ye Legation' (NARA M31 reel 12 frames 0362-0367; Founders Madison/99-01-02-1993)

documents.shelfmark: NARA RG 59, Despatches from US Ministers to Spain, vol. 10 = microfilm M31 reel 12 frames 0362-0367 (NAID 188605361), the duplicate

plaintext.source: Founders Online early-access text 99-01-02-1993 (Papers of James Madison): the letter decoded, without the code groups, with ten blank gaps; source given as DNA RG 59 DD Spain; how the code was decoded is not stated.

transcription.source: NARA M31 reel 12 frames 0362-0367 via catalog.archives.gov (NAID 188605361)
transcription.notes: Measured with --drop-first on groups.txt (from aligned.txt). distinct counts caret (^) and hidden-digit (#) spellings separately; the letter has 395 distinct numbers. The transcription has 1,147 positions once the repeated acceptance passage (0362.3b = 0363L.1) is counted once: two uncertain positions on frame 0367 have no aligned group. 37 groups have digits partly hidden in the binding. OpenAI Codex re-read 53 groups on the images (purposive sample): 0 digit mismatches.

system.summary: Numerical word-and-syllable code of the American legation at Madrid (Pinckney's 'Cypher of the Legation'; the = 1651, of = 133, to = 244), groups up to about 1,700 joined by dots inside clear text, a caret over a group for the plural.

diacritics.note: a caret or small triangle over a group marks a plural (424^ ions, 580^ ports)

system.sibling_key: Pinckney's despatch of 22 Feb 1803 with Jacob Wagner's interlinear decode (M31 reel 7 frame 0348) and the pairs of Erving's 24 Mar 1807 letter (targets/erving1807); used as checks, 45 of 47 shared groups compatible with Wagner.
system.notes: entries = rows of the rebuilt key (395 numbers of this letter, 19 from Wagner's page). Alphabetical runs: 742-745 at/ate/ated/ation, 870-880 their...thing, 1340/1341/1343 an/ance/and; the order breaks higher up. Erving's slips: 66 for in (x3), 665 for 605, 870 for they, 943 for 934 in Hanover (x2).

prior_solution.where: Founders Online early-access document 99-01-02-1993 prints the letter decoded, with ten blank gaps; the groups, the key and the decoding route are not given.

conditions.human_role: Outside contribution (Feyseel Nur, PR #21): chose the target from the 'Not done' item in targets/erving1807/NOTES.md, ran Claude Opus 5.5 subagents for transcription, key rebuild and decode, and commissioned an adversarial review by OpenAI Codex; the write-up applies the review's corrections. No hand correction of readings recorded.
tools: alignment of code groups with the Founders text (aligned.txt)

solution.what: Checked Founders Online for the 10 Aug 1807 letter flagged in targets/erving1807/NOTES.md: early-access 99-01-02-1993 prints it decoded, with ten blank gaps, citing RG 59 DD Spain.
Fetched M31 reel 12 frames 0358-0370 (NAID 188605361) and reel 7 frames 0346-0349 (NAID 188604008) from catalog.archives.gov.
Transcribed the code groups of frames 0362-0367 with the clear words between them (transcription.txt).
Aligned every group with the Founders text at its place (aligned.txt, 1,145 groups) and built the key (414 rows); values carried to every other occurrence and tested there.
Compared the key with Jacob Wagner's 1803 interlinear decode of Pinckney's despatch (reel 7 frame 0348): 47 shared group numbers, 45 compatible, 584 and 943 indeterminate.

Decoded the letter and the postscript (reading.txt); six of Founders' ten blank gaps filled from values that recur outside the gaps, one plausible, two speculative, one shown to hide no code; three disagreements with the Founders text.

Adversarial review by OpenAI Codex (codex_review/): confirmed but overstated; 716 tokens (62.5%) with outside support, 908 (79.3%) with recurrence or outside support; 53 sampled groups match the images; conservative sensitivity count 1,081/1,147 = 94.25%.

outcome.method: key recovered based on plaintext from external sources
outcome.method_basis: Key rebuilt by aligning the 1,145 code groups of the NARA duplicate with the decoded text printed in Founders Online (early access 99-01-02-1993), then checked against Jacob Wagner's 1803 decode of Pinckney's despatch in the same code (45 of 47 shared groups compatible).
outcome.fraction_read_source: aligned.txt: 1,145 code groups; X counted unread (9); fraction_coherent also drops the 11 values marked ? (1,125/1,145). Over the transcription's 1,147 positions: 1,125 = 0.981. Codex's conservative sensitivity count (codex_review/metrics.json): 1,081/1,147 = 0.9425.

outcome.notes: Extent complete on the nominal count (98.3% give sense without conjectures). Codex: confirmed but overstated; a conservative count that also drops 37 hidden-digit restorations and nine emendations is 94.25%, below 95%, so the extent depends on accepting disclosed restorations and emendations. Grades are not counted token by token: values are C from the Founders text, M for the doubtful ones and I for hidden-digit restorations and EXPECTATIONS (NOTES, Uncertain readings). Founders' decoded text existed before; whether it was made from this duplicate is not settled.
